sentences.text:
Pratik Mohan @ Prateek Mohan vs Unknown on 20 January,
2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
20.01.2023 Srimanta Crr/221/2023

In the matter of : Pratik Mohan @ Prateek Mohan Ankur &
Anr.

Mr. Sandipan Ganguly, Sr. Adv., Mr. Ayan Bhattaharjee, Adv., Mr. Kausik De, Adv., Ms. Mohini
Mazumdar, Adv., Ms. Kriti Mehrotra, Adv., Mr. Raghav Munshi, Adv., ...for the petitioners.
The petitioners are the employees of Hotel Holiday Inn situated within the jurisdiction of Baguiati Police Station.

On the basis of written complaint submitted by the opposite party no. 2 the jurisdictional Police Station registered a case against the petitioners under Sections 406/420/420B/336 of the Indian Penal Code.
In order to appreciate the dispute it is necessary to record the following background as a prologue.

On the basis of a memorandum of understanding between Holiday Inn, Kolkata Airport and Raj Kumar Jaiswal, proprietor of V.R. Entertainment an evening party was scheduled to be conducted with food, drinks and songs at the said Hotel premises.
The tickets of the said program were sold from online channel under the name and style of 'Book My Show'.
The de facto complainant/opposite party no. 2 purchased two tickets for herself and her husband paying Rs.4,000/-.
It is alleged that there were absolute mismanagement in the said program.
The invitees were not offered with proper food.
They were furious.
Some of them broke the articles in the kitchen of the said Hotel.
Even alcoholic drinks were not properly distributed and a mess was created in the said Hotel.
It is also alleged that the opposite party no. 2 was duped and deceived by the Hotel authority and being deceived as such she parted with a sum of Rs.4,000/-.
Accordingly, Police registered a case under Sections 420/406 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the petitioners are mere employees of the Hotel.
Even assuming that there was rush of invitees, there was some mismanagement by the Hotel authorities and the employees cannot be held liable for this.
The petitioners have annexed some CCTV footage of the said program.
On perusal of which this Court does not prima facie find any rush or mismanagement in the said program.
Be that as it may for the act of the management of Hotel Holiday Inn, Kolkata Airport the individual employees cannot be held liable.
Moreover from the memorandum of understanding executed by and between Holiday Inn and V.R. Entertainment it is ascertained that the entire event was managed by V.R. Entertainment.
In view of such circumstances, the instant revision is admitted.

sentences.text: Petitioners are directed to serve notice upon the private opposite parties under registered speed post with acknowledgement due and file affidavit-of-service within a period of three weeks from the date of this order.

The State of West Bengal be served through the learned Public Prosecutor, High Court,
Calcutta.
In the meantime, the Investigating Officer shall not take any coercive step against the petitioners.

It is also submitted on behalf of the petitioners that under the garb of investigation the Investigating authority has sealed all marriage Banquet Halls of Hotel Holiday Inn under the name and style of Darbar, Onyx etc.
It is also submitted that the provision of Section 102 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not include immovable property.
Thus, Section 102 does not empower the Police Officer to seize immovable property in course of investigation.
In support of his contention he refers to Nevada Properties Pvt. Ltd. through its Directors -Vs.- State of Maharashtra & Anr. reported in (2019) 20 SCC 119.

The Investigating authority is directed to take videography of Darbar Hall and Onyx before opening the said Halls and after obtaining the videography the said Banquet Halls will be opened and the possession thereof will be delivered to the management of Holiday Inn within 48 hours of communication of this order.
Petitioners are at liberty to act on the server copy of the order.
[ ( Bibek Chaudhuri, J. )
